messages:
sara_support: hey team, seeing a spike in streaming TTFB p95/p99 for a single customer since last night's infra deploy. non-streaming (batch) endpoints are fine. customer reports p95 ~1.8s, previously ~200ms.

alex_infra: thanks — can you drop a request id and sample headers? is the client using h2 or http/1.1?

sara_support: req id r-9f3b2a. client uses http/2 from their edge; our path: client -> envoy edge -> internal h2 pool -> sidecar/runtime. sample headers:

```:method: POST
:scheme: https
:authority: api.customer.net
content-type: application/json
te: trailers
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-request-id: r-9f3b2a
```

jin_prod: grabbed proxy and runtime logs for r-9f3b2a. runtime is emitting tokens immediately but writes to the sidecar/runtime socket are tiny (5–20 bytes). envoy is coalescing those tiny writes and only flushing after ~200ms. timeline from proxy logs:

```
[09:12:01.120] runtime -> proxy write 18 bytes
[09:12:01.121] runtime -> proxy write 12 bytes
[09:12:01.321] proxy flush to client (coalesced 11 writes)
```

so there's ~200ms gap between tiny writes and the actual flush to client; that explains TTFB regression for streaming while total time isn't impacted.

maria_engineering: we rolled a sidecar change last night that bumped our HTTP library and introduced a gzip middleware. PR 4723 modified buffer behavior (default 256B) and enabled gzip for responses. small token outputs get buffered until buffer full or a timer fires. could be the cause. i'll diff the release.

chris_ce: customer repro: they toggled streaming off (?stream=false) and p95 stays low, so it's specific to chunked/streaming path.

alex_infra: likely suspects: (1) middleware buffer/gzip, (2) http2 flow-control/settings causing manual coalescing, (3) TCP Nagle (TCP_NODELAY), or (4) envoy per-connection flush heuristics.

maria_engineering: confirmed — PR added compress middleware that buffers up to 256 bytes and flushes on res.end or when timer hits. tiny token writes never reach threshold, so they wait on flush timer (~200ms).

sara_support: good catch. can we reproduce locally to be certain?

jin_prod: repro steps I ran: 1) curl -N -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://staging.api.redwood.internal/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"short"}' 2) tcpdump between runtime and sidecar: `tcpdump -i lo -w smallwrites.pcap` 3) observe many small writes then single flush at ~200ms. hexdump shows tiny token payloads (6–12 bytes) separated by silence then coalesced flush.

maria_engineering: short-term fix: change gzip to streaming mode or disable buffering for streaming routes. immediate patch: set `gzip.buffer_limit = 0` for streaming routes and call `res.flush()` after each `res.write(chunk)` in the runtime adapter. opening a canary PR now.

alex_infra: mitigation at edge: create per-route config to disable compression for `/v1/stream` and add `per_route.socket_options: tcp_nodelay: true`. that can reduce proxy-side coalescing for smaller writes.

maria_engineering: opened PR 4750 to disable gzip for streaming routes and add explicit flushes. will canary to 5% first.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: sidecar-image:v2.8.4-canary -> 5% traffic (id: canary-2026-03-15-09)

sara_support: notified customer with a workaround (use non-streaming or `sse=true` param). they're going to test the canary tomorrow.

chris_ce: docs note suggestion: "If streaming TTFB regresses but overall completion time is stable, check for middleware compression buffering and proxy coalescing. Use `curl -N` and tcpdump between runtime and sidecar to confirm small writes are being buffered.' :memo:

maria_engineering: internal tests on canary show p95 improved from ~1.8s -> ~230ms for streaming. promoting to 50% in 30m if stable.

maria_engineering: follow-up — added a small repro harness under `eng-runtime/stream-repro/` that emits many tiny token writes to exercise gzip and flush behavior. repository link: https://git.internal.redwood/eng-runtime/stream-repro

sara_support: will close with customer once rollout confirms improvement. :thumbsup:
